statement: You are given an array dims of length n + 1 describing a chain of n matrices: matrix i, for 1 ≤ i ≤ n, has dimensions dims[i − 1] × dims[i].
Multiplying an a × b matrix by a b × c matrix costs a × b × c scalar multiplications. The product of the whole chain is the same however it is parenthesised, but the cost is not.
Return the smallest total number of scalar multiplications needed to multiply the whole chain.

examples.explanation: Multiplying left to right, ((A × B) × C) × D, costs 6000 + 12000 + 12000 = 30000, the cheapest order for these four matrices.
There are only two matrices, 10 × 20 and 20 × 30, so the one product costs 10 × 20 × 30 = 6000.

Multiplying left to right costs 6·2·9 + 6·9·3 + 6·3·7 = 108 + 162 + 126 = 396. Multiplying B·C first (2·9·3 = 54), then that by D (2·3·7 = 42), then A by the result (6·2·7 = 84) costs only 180 - the order changes the work by more than half.
